validity.recommendation: Keep as operating; swap Status refs to the 2020 SGGP pigging page and the 2021 Waha Oil wayback article (both stronger/more contemporary than the weak 2017 'presumed' basis GEM's own wiki page admits to).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/STATUS: Real pipeline, independently confirmed by THREE separate origins: (1) eanlibya.com (Ain Libya news, 2017-07-22) reports a Presidential Council meeting on resuming the 'Intisar–Sarir' gas transmission pipeline project (contractor Petrojet, consultant firm Brand), stalled since 2014, with agreement to resume/complete work by August 2017 — this is the SAME source gem.wiki cites for status/start-year, and gem.wiki's own Background section literally states 'There is no direct evidence that the pipeline is operating, but this is the presumed status given an agreement that occurred in 2017' — i.e. GEM itself flags this as unproven. (2) sirtggp.com (Sirt Gulf Gas Projects Co., a Libyan gas-pipeline-services company) has a dated project page for pigging/cleaning the '20-inch Intisar–Sarir pipeline, 114 km', contracted 2020-02-11 — routine pigging maintenance on a named, in-service line is strong evidence it was actually operating by 2020, independent of the shaky 2017 basis. (3) wahaoil.ly (Waha Oil Co.'s own site, archived via Wayback since the live site is now Cloudflare-gated) describes a 2021-01-04 incident where a CPU/compressor fault at Al-Fareg field cut gas supply to 'khat haql al-Intisar (A) wa mahattat al-Sarir' (the Intisar(A) field-and-Sarir-station line) for two days, then restored to full capacity — this both names the same route and confirms active operation as of Jan 2021. Together these upgrade the pipeline from GEM's own admitted 'presumed' status to a well-evidenced 'confirmed (caveat)' — caveat being that it evidently sat unfinished/stalled 2014–2017 before entering service, so 'operating' should not be read as continuous since an early date.

validity.recommendation: Verify Owner: two independent sources put the transmission pipeline itself under 'al-Sharikah al-'Ammah li-Naql wa Tawzi' al-Ghaz' (General Company for Gas Transmission and Distribution), with Petrojet as EPC contractor — not the Waha Oil consortium GEM currently lists as Owner1-4. Operator=Waha Oil Co. is separately well-supported (Waha's own site describes running gas supply/compression into this exact line), so Operator may be right even if Owner needs reconciling.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists Owner1-4 as the Waha Oil Co. concession partners (Libyan NOC 59.18%, ConocoPhillips 16.33%, TotalEnergies SE 16.33%, Hess Corp 8.16% — sums to 100%, and is the well-known, publicly reported Waha/Concession-59 ownership split). But the eanlibya.com 2017 article names 'al-Sharikah al-'Ammah li-Naql wa Tawzi' al-Ghaz' (General Co. for Gas Transmission & Distribution) as the entity whose board chairman (Mohamed Salem) and planning director attended the meeting to negotiate resuming the pipeline's construction, alongside contractor Petrojet and consultant firm Brand — i.e. this state gas-transmission company, not Waha, appears to be the party responsible for building/owning the transmission asset. The sirtggp.com 2020 project page independently corroborates this, explicitly listing 'al-jihah al-malikah' (the owning entity) for the pigging job as the same 'al-Sharikah al-'Ammah li-Naql wa Tawzi' al-Ghaz'. I could not find independent confirmation this pass that the Waha consortium (vs. the gas-transmission company) is the correct Owner for the pipeline asset itself — the Waha percentages are almost certainly correct for the Waha OIL FIELD/concession, but may have been carried over to the pipeline record without verifying the pipeline's actual owner. Flagging for reconciliation rather than asserting GEM is wrong outright, since GEM's Operator field (Waha Oil Co.) is independently supported by Waha's own site describing their role feeding gas into this line.

validity.recommendation: Reconcile Length: independent, dated maintenance-contract source states 114 km for the 20-inch Intisar–Sarir line, vs. GEM's 235 km — verify origin of the 235 km figure or correct to ~114 km. Also review ConstructionYear=2014 and StartYear1=2017: the only source found for either date describes 2014 as when construction WORK STOPPED (not started) and 2017 as an agreement-to-resume-work date (not a confirmed in-service date), so both fields may be recording the wrong milestone.
validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH: sirtggp.com's 2020 project page titles the job 'Pigging of the Intisar–Sarir pipeline, 20 inch, at a distance of 114 km' ('...20 بوصة على بعد 114 كم'). Diameter (20 in) matches GEM exactly, which makes this a credible, specific, on-the-nose match for the same asset — but the stated length (114 km) is roughly HALF of GEM's recorded 235 km. This is a material disagreement per a source that otherwise corroborates the pipeline precisely (same name, same diameter), so it can't be waved off as describing a different line. DATES: eanlibya.com (2017-07-22) says the Petrojet-built Intisar–Sarir gas transmission line project had been 'stopped since 2014' ('توقف منذ سنة 2014') and that attendees agreed to set up a mechanism to resume and complete work 'during the upcoming month of August' 2017 — i.e. as of the article, the line was NOT yet confirmed operating; 2017 marks an agreement-to-resume-construction, not a verified start-of-service. GEM's ConstructionYear=2014 plausibly derives from this same source but conflates 'construction paused' with 'construction began'; StartYear1=2017 likewise reflects the resume-agreement date rather than a confirmed operational start (matching gem.wiki's own hedge that 2017 is merely 'presumed'). Neither date is independently corroborated as the CORRECT milestone by a second source in this pass.

fills.researcher_notes: eanlibya.com repeatedly refers to this as 'khat naql al-ghaz' (gas transmission line) feeding a gas power station ('mahattat al-Sarir al-ghaziyah') — unambiguous confirmation of Fuel=Gas.

Both sources independently name the route as 'Intisar–Sarir' ('khat Intisar–Sarir' / 'khat naql al-ghaz al-Intisar–Sarir'), consistent with Start=Intisar (Sirte Basin) and End=Sarir (Cyrenaica). Note the sources describe the endpoint as 'mahattat al-Sarir' (Sarir station/plant) rather than explicitly 'Sarir oil field' — same area, but EndLocation label could be tightened to 'Sarir gas station' if more precision is wanted.

Waha Oil Co.'s own site (archived, live site now behind Cloudflare) describes its own Engineering and Al-Fareg field Operations departments restoring gas supply to the Intisar(A)-field/Sarir-station line — directly supports Operator=Waha Oil Co. for the gas-supply/compression side of this pipeline. See attribution concern re: the transmission asset itself possibly belonging to a different (state gas-transmission) company.

This is the article's own date (2017-07-22) and the only source found tying the pipeline to that year — but it reports an AGREEMENT to resume/complete construction 'during August' 2017, not a confirmed in-service date. Providing this ref restores traceability for the existing 2017 value, but it should be read as weak/presumed (matching gem.wiki's own hedge), not as firm confirmation — see spec concern.

The only 2014-linked source found (eanlibya.com, 2017) says the pipeline project had been STOPPED since 2014, not that construction began then. Did not find a source confirming an actual construction-start year, so left unresolved rather than pairing a ref that would misrepresent what it supports — see spec concern for detail.

This split matches the well-known Waha Oil Co./Concession-59 ownership structure, but I could not independently verify it as the correct Owner for the PIPELINE ASSET this pass (web search budget was exhausted mid-task) — and two sources instead point to a different midstream owner for the transmission line itself. See attribution concern; left unresolved rather than fabricate a supporting citation.

summary: Intisar–Sarir Gas Pipeline is real and independently confirmed operating (upgrading GEM's own 'presumed' status via a 2020 SGGP pigging record and a 2021 Waha Oil supply-restoration notice), but two concerns: Owner may belong to a state gas-transmission company rather than the Waha consortium GEM lists, and Length (235 km) conflicts with an independent, diameter-matching source stating 114 km; ConstructionYear/StartYear also look like they may record the wrong milestone (halt vs. start; agreement-to-resume vs. completion).
